title: Cross-Jurisdictional Enforcement of Invalid Sanctions — International Corporate Enforcement Without Validation
category: International Aviation / Human Rights / Treaty Law

incident.date: 2024-04-04 (GRU precursor incident — pre-ban) and 2024-07-05 (SCL primary incident — removal + ban creation)
incident.location: Santiago International Airport (SCL), Chile and Guarulhos International Airport (GRU), Brazil

incident_timestamp_display: 2024-04-04 (GRU precursor incident — pre-ban) and 2024-07-05 (SCL primary incident — removal + ban creation)
allegation_summary: LATAM Airlines Brazil (TAM Linhas Aéreas) imposed a lifetime flight ban on passenger [[SPK-passenger-leandro]] in Chile based on disproven allegations of aggression. The ban was subsequently enforced by LATAM Brazil at Guarulhos International Airport (GRU) on April 4, 2025, without any independent validation of the underlying allegations. Brazilian airport authorities facilitated this enforcement. This cross-jurisdictional enforcement of an invalid corporate sanction violates multiple international law principles: (a) the obligation to validate foreign administrative/contractual sanctions before enforcing them; (b) the Montreal Convention's jurisdictional framework (Articles 33 and 46); (c) international consumer protection standards against abusive cross-border practices; and (d) Brazilian sovereignty through the automatic enforcement of a foreign private corporation's decision without domestic review.

articles.article_name: Article 33: An action for damages must be brought, at the option of the plaintif
articles.article_text: 1. An action for damages must be brought, at the option of the plaintiff, in the territory of one of the States Parties, either before the court of the domicile of the carrier or of its principal place of business, or where it has a place of business through which the contract has been made or before the court at the place of destination. 2. In respect of damage resulting from the death or injury of a passenger, an action may be brought before one of the courts mentioned in paragraph 1 of this Article, or in the territory of a State Party in which at the time of the accident the passenger has his or her principal and permanent residence and to or from which the carrier operates services for the carriage of passengers by air, either on its own aircraft, or on another carrier's aircraft pursuant to a commercial agreement, and in which that carrier conducts its business of carriage of passengers by air from premises leased or owned by the carrier itself or by another carrier with which it has a commercial agreement. 3. For the purposes of paragraph 2, (a) "commercial agreement" means an agreement, other than an agency agreement, made between carriers and relating to the provision of their joint services for carriage of passengers by air; (b) "principal and permanent residence" means the one fixed and permanent abode of the passenger at the time of the accident. The nationality of the passenger shall not be the determining factor in this regard. 4. Questions of procedure shall be governed by the law of the court seized of the case.
articles.applicability_rationale: legacy paraphrase: Article 33: An action for damages must be brought, at the option of the plaintiff, in the territory of one of the States Parties, either before the court of the domicile of the carrier, or where the contract was made, or at the place of destination.

articles.article_name: Article 46: Additional jurisdiction — action may be brought against the actual c
articles.article_text: Any action for damages contemplated in Article 45 must be brought, at the option of the plaintiff, in the territory of one of the States Parties, either before a court in which an action may be brought against the contracting carrier, as provided in Article 33, or before the court having jurisdiction at the place where the actual carrier has its domicile or its principal place of business.
articles.applicability_rationale: legacy paraphrase: Article 46: Additional jurisdiction — action may be brought against the actual carrier at its domicile or principal place of business.
